# Create a document and edit properties

Open a document, add a typed length and an enumeration, write a value through each, and see the error an invalid enumeration value raises.

> **Generated page.** `tools/userdocs.py` writes it from
> [`tools/workflows/01_documents_and_properties.py`](../../../tools/workflows/01_documents_and_properties.py).
> Edit the workflow, not this page; `python3 tools/userdocs.py --check`
> fails when the two disagree.

**Requires:** the `FreeCAD` facade; no workbench module and no GPU.

## 1. Create a document

`newDocument` registers the document with the application and makes it active. The registry lives in the Rust core, so the facade keeps no state of its own.

```python
doc = FreeCAD.newDocument('Demo')
```

| Read back | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Active document | Demo |
| Open documents | ["Demo"] |

## 2. Add properties

A feature object is created by type name. Properties are added one at a time and carry a group and a description, which is what a property editor shows. `App::PropertyLength` is a quantity, so it accepts a unit string and formats a value back with a unit.

```python
part = doc.addObject("App::FeaturePython", "Part")
part.addProperty("App::PropertyLength", "Length", "Base", "Overall length")
part.addProperty("App::PropertyEnumeration", "Finish", "Base", "Surface finish")
part.Finish = ["As machined", "Anodised"]
```

```python
part.Length = "10 mm"
part.Finish = "Anodised"
```

| Read back | Value |
| --- | --- |
| part.Length | 10 mm |
| part.Finish | Anodised |
| Property types | ["Finish", "Length"] |

## 3. An invalid value is rejected

The enumeration is a closed set. Assigning a value outside it raises `ValueError` and leaves the property unchanged; a script can rely on that instead of validating the set itself.

```python
try:
    part.Finish = "Bogus"
except ValueError as exc:
    rejected = str(exc)
```

| Read back | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Error | "Bogus" is not part of the enumeration |
| part.Finish is unchanged | Anodised |

## 4. Close the document

Closing unregisters the document from the application.

```python
FreeCAD.closeDocument('Demo')
```

| Read back | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Open documents | [] |

> The values above are read from the live object, not from a fixture: this page is generated by running the script in `tools/workflows/`.
